During training, apprentices are entitled to free medical treatment only from the Naval Dockyard Dispensary, limited to the facility available there. The period of training is as per Rule 7 and Schedule I of the Apprentices Rules 1992.

Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Reservation Policy

  • Reservation for SC and ST is as per Schedule II A of the Apprentice Rules, 1992, and for OBC (NCL) as per Maharashtra Act No. VIII of 2004.
  • Reserved vacancies are filled separately from eligible SC, ST and OBC candidates, who are either lower in merit than the last candidate on the merit list of the UR category or SC/ST/OBC (NCL) candidates who have availed age relaxation, irrespective of their position in the merit list.
  • Reserved vacancies for PwBD and ESM are filled from eligible candidates of the respective category who are lower in merit than the last candidate on the merit list of that category but otherwise found suitable for appointment even by relaxed standard.
  • PwBD and ESM reservations are horizontal and cut across the vertical SC/ST/OBC(NCL) reservation (inter-locking reservation). Candidates selected against PwBD and ESM quota are placed in the appropriate category of UR/SC/ST/OBC(NCL), as the case may be.
  • PwBD reservation follows MSDE-4/3/2023-AP(PMU) dated 11 Apr 25 regarding applicability of the RPwD Act 2016 to ATS and trade-wise suitability of PwBD.
  • Persons with SD/SI with associated limb dysfunction are covered under the respective sub-category of LD, as the case may be.

Horizontal reservation for Ex-Servicemen categories applies to the following, as per Para 3.6.3 of the Apprenticeship Training Manual:

  1. Children of deceased/disabled Ex-Servicemen including those killed/disabled during peace time
  2. Children of Ex-Servicemen
  3. Children of Serving Jawans
  4. Children of Serving Officers
  5. Ex-Servicemen

Abbreviations used in the notification: UR – Unreserved; SC – Scheduled Caste; ST – Scheduled Tribes; OBC (NCL) – Other Backward Class (Non Creamy Layer); PwBD – Person with Benchmark Disabilities; ESM – Ex-Serviceman.

Suitable Groups of Benchmark Disability for PwBD

Physical requirement suitability for PwBDs is as identified by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment notification No. 38-16-2020-DD-III dated 04 Jan 2021, amended vide notification No. 30-12/2020-DD-III dated 24 Aug 2022.

Group Disability Categories
Group A LD, CP, LC, DW, AAV
Group B B, LV
Group C D, HH
Group D ASD (M, MOD), ID, SLD, MI
Group E MD

Abbreviations: LD – Locomotor Disability; CP – Cerebral Palsy; LC – Leprosy Cured; DW – Dwarfism; AAV – Acid Attack Victims; B – Blindness; LV – Low Vision; D – Deaf; HH – Hard of Hearing; ASD (M, MoD) – Autism Spectrum Disorder (Mild, Moderate); ID – Intellectual Disability; SLD – Specific Learning Disability; MI – Mental Illness; MD – Multiple Disabilities; SD – Spinal Deformity; SI – Spinal Injury. PwBD candidates must hold a disability certificate issued by the Competent Authority, in the prescribed format under Rule 18(1) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Notification G.S.R 591(E) dated 15 Jun 2017, before applying online. The format is available on the portal under Important Documents. To avail reservation, the certificate must show 40% or above disability.

Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Physical Standards

Candidates should satisfy the minimum standards of physical fitness under Rule A and Schedule II of the Apprentices Rules 1992:

  • Free from Tuberculosis, contagious/infectious diseases and any disease likely to be aggravated by service causing danger to public health.
  • Height: 137 cms minimum. Weight: 25.4 Kgs minimum. Chest expansion: 3.8 cms minimum.
  • Eyes: free from morbidity of either eye or eyelids.
  • Free from any other chronic illness of the Alimentary System, Cardio Vascular, Respiratory System, Genito-Urinary System, Skeletal System, Nervous System, Glandular System, Ears, Skin and Speech.

Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Selection Process

Selection is carried out as per extant guidelines of the Competent Authority. The stages are as follows.

  • Screening of applications: Naval Dockyard Mumbai will not carry out detailed scrutiny of online applications before the examination. Detailed scrutiny of documents is done at a subsequent stage.
  • Shortlisting: Fulfilling the basic criteria does not automatically entitle a candidate to the written examination. If applications are too many in proportion to vacancies, the authority may shortlist applications, in the ratio of 1:25 for every available vacancy in each trade and category.
  • Merit calculation: Equal weightage (50:50) is given to marks in Class 10th from a recognised Board and marks in the ITI consolidated statement of marks for AITT issued by NCVET. For Crane Operator (SI), 100% weightage is given to Class 10th. For Rigger, 100% weightage is given to Class 8th.
  • Written examination: Objective type, OMR format, as described below.
  • Medical examination: Selected candidates must submit a medical fitness certificate from a Government hospital before being engaged, as per Rule 4 and Schedule II of the Apprentices Rules.
  • Document verification: Original documents uploaded on the portal are verified by Dockyard Apprentice School. Dates for verification and joining are intimated by email to selected candidates.

Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Exam Pattern

The written test has 100 questions of one mark each, is bilingual (English and Hindi), and its questions match the Class 10th standard syllabus for all trades except Rigger, which follows the 8th standard syllabus. The exam is likely to be held on one day in one shift for all trades. Details of negative marking are not specified in the notification.

S. No. Subject Maximum Marks Duration
1 General Science 35 02 Hours
2 Mathematics 35
3 General Knowledge 30
  Total 100

The exact date, time and venue are communicated to shortlisted candidates on registered email IDs and through the portal. The e-admit card must be downloaded from the portal. The exam is to be conducted in Mumbai and its suburban districts such as Thane, Kandivali etc.

Resolution of Ties

  1. Marks in the written examination are considered first.
  2. If written exam marks are the same, the older candidate (by date of birth) ranks higher.
  3. If date of birth is also the same, alphabetical order of the first name is considered.

Scribe Facility

  • PwBD candidates with disability of 40% and above: A scribe is given to candidates with blindness, locomotor disability (both arms affected – BA) and cerebral palsy if desired. For other benchmark disabilities, a certificate of physical limitation to write and need of a scribe is required from the Chief Medical Officer / Civil Surgeon / Medical Superintendent of a Government health care institution (Appendix I, MoSJE OM 34-02/2015-DD-III dated 29 Aug 2018). If the candidate brings their own scribe, the scribe's qualification must be one step below the candidate's, and details are submitted in the proforma at Appendix II of the same OM.
  • PwD candidates with disability less than 40%: Scribe and/or compensatory time is granted only to those having difficulty in writing, on a certificate from the competent medical authority of a Government health care institution (Appendix I, MoSJE OM F. No. 29-6/2019-DD-III dated 10 Aug 2022). Own-scribe rules are the same, with the proforma at Appendix II of that OM.
  • PwBD candidates with medical categories other than blindness, locomotor disability (both arms affected – BA) and cerebral palsy, who need a scribe, must carry the relevant original medical certificate to the examination, failing which the scribe and compensatory time may not be allowed.

Documents Required for Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Candidates should keep scanned copies ready before filling the online application:

  • Passport-size colour photograph on a plain white background, not more than three months old, with full face coverage, no cap or goggles, both ears visible. Size 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm, jpeg/jpg, 50–100 Kb.
  • Signature in black ink on plain white paper (scanned copy of own signature, not digitised), jpeg/jpg, 50–100 Kb.
  • Birth Certificate/Matriculation certificate for date of birth (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • Aadhaar as proof of identity, in pdf (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • Trades other than Rigger: Matriculation certificate in pdf (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • Rigger: Birth Certificate and Class VIIIth marksheet (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • The 30 ITI trades: ITI certificate (mandatory) and consolidated (all semesters) ITI marks in pdf (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • Caste certificate, if applying against a reserved post, in pdf (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • Certificate showing disability for PwBD, if applicable, in pdf (not exceeding 400 Kb).
  • Certificate of proof of Ex-Servicemen / certificate of son/daughter of Armed Forces Personnel issued by the Competent Authority, in pdf (not exceeding 400 Kb).

How to Apply for Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Naval Dockyard Mumbai Apprentice Apply Online

  1. Visit https://www.apprenticeshipregistration.com and download the online application guidelines before filling in the form.
  2. Check that you meet the educational qualification and other criteria. Candidates from a Board or institution using the grade point system must get grade points converted into percentage of marks by the appropriate authority, or use a conversion chart from the respective Board. If unavailable, the lowest percentage of the grade point will be considered for shortlisting.
  3. Keep your valid and active email ID and mobile number ready. No change in the email ID or mobile number is allowed once entered.
  4. Write your Name and Date of Birth strictly as given in the matriculation certificate. Otherwise the candidature may be cancelled.
  5. Upload the photograph, signature and documents listed above in the required formats and sizes.
  6. Remember the password set during registration; further login is possible only with it.
  7. Submit the application within the registration window and take a printout of the application form for personal record. No copy needs to be sent anywhere.
  8. Download the E-admit card from the portal when released.

Candidates may apply for more than one designated trade in the same application. The examination centre for each may be one or different and may fall on the same day/shift. If two trades fall in the same shift, the candidate can appear for only one trade of his/her choice. If two exams are in different shifts on the same day, the candidate must reach the allotted centre.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Previous training: Candidates undergoing apprenticeship in any Govt./Public Sector/Private industrial organisation must terminate their ongoing contract through the MSDE Portal before applying, and must have fulfilled any cooling down criterion if applicable.
  • Multiple applications: Do not submit multiple applications. If more than one is submitted, the one with the higher application number, if complete in all respects, is the only one considered.
  • Provisional candidature: Applications are accepted provisionally. False or incorrect information leads to cancellation without prejudice to legal action.
  • Caste certificates: SC/ST candidates must hold a latest caste certificate and produce the original on demand. OBC candidates must produce a valid caste certificate stating they do not belong to the creamy layer, in the format under GoI DoP&T OM 36033/1/2013-Estt(Res) dated 27 May 2013 and 36036/2/2013-Estt.(Res) dated 30 May 2014. If the OBC(NCL) certificate is not in the prescribed format or outside its validity period, the candidate is treated as General.
  • Applying early: Apply well before the closing date. Naval Dockyard Mumbai is not responsible for mistakes in the online application or for non-receipt of communication on the registered mobile number/email.
  • At the exam centre: Carry the admit card and an original photo ID (passport / Aadhaar / Driving licence / Govt. issued ID). Late reporting after the time on the admit card is not permitted. The name on the admit card is as per the matriculation certificate (Class VIIIth mark sheet for Rigger). If the name was changed and published in the official gazette after Class 10, a copy of the gazette must be given to the invigilator. Check the admit card for discrepancies before the exam; no correspondence is entertained after the examination.
  • Exam conduct: Mobiles and electronic gadgets are banned in the premises, even in switch-off mode. Companions are not allowed at the venue or in its proximity. Candidates must arrange their own lodging/boarding and avoid bringing valuables.
  • Results: Results of the written examination are published online through the portal. The option of opting out of personal information must be exercised at the time of filling up the online application.
  • Hostel: Limited hostel facility for boys only, allocated on merit with first preference to outstation candidates; if vacant, it may be extended to local candidates (proof of current address required). There is no hostel or lodging facility for female candidates.
  • Employment after training: Naval Dockyard Mumbai is not obliged to offer employment after training, and the apprentice is not obliged to accept. Ex-Naval Apprentices can apply for Tradesman Skilled in Naval Dockyards per recruitment rules, subject to the upper age limit for that post, which also applies to those applying for Tradesman Skilled in the Indian Navy.
  • Updates: Check the portal regularly for updates, corrigendum and further instructions. Orders, circulars and formats of certificates are available on the portal under Reference Documents.
  • Queries and grievances: Send queries to the help desk email [email protected] within seven days of uploading of the provisionally eligible merit list for written examination and the provisional select list. No queries are accepted after the seven days. The notification also prints Helpdesk Number 971842361.

Action Against Misconduct

Candidates found guilty of the following can be summarily cancelled at any stage of enrolment, apart from criminal action, and debarred from Naval Dockyard Mumbai examinations for the period below. The Naval Dockyard can also cancel candidature on any other ground it considers sufficient, or for any irregular or improper means.

Type of Malpractice Debarment Period
Seating at a place other than the designated place 03 Years
Taking away examination material such as question paper, answer sheet, rough sheets, Naval Dockyard's copy of attendance sheet, or passing it to unauthorised persons 03 Years
Making incorrect or false statements, suppressing material information, submitting fabricated, forged or tampered documents 03 Years
Obtaining support or influence by irregular or improper means 03 Years
Possession of a mobile phone in 'switched on' or 'switched off mode' 03 Years
Misbehaving, intimidating or threatening examination functionaries (Supervisor, Invigilator, Security Guard or Naval Dockyard representatives) 05 Years
Creating nuisance or disturbance at the exam centre, obstructing the examination or instigating others not to take it 05 Years
A candidate who is also working on examination related matters in the same examination 05 Years
Damaging examination related infrastructure/equipment 05 Years
Appearing in the exam with forged admit card, identity proof, etc. 05 Years
Using unfair means such as copying from unauthorised sources (written material on paper or body parts) 05 Years
Impersonation by or on behalf of the candidate 07 Years
Possession of Bluetooth devices, spy cameras or other electronic gadgets in the examination hall 07 Years
Taking snapshots or making videos of question papers or examination material, labs etc. 07 Years
Sharing examination terminal through remote desktop software/Apps/LAN 07 Years
Attempt to hack or manipulate examination servers, data and systems before, during or after the examination 07 Years
Possession of fire arms/weapons during the examination 07 Years

Caution to All Candidates

The notification warns candidates to beware of touts and job racketeers who may falsely promise selection for illegal consideration. Selection is purely on merit, no money is required to be paid to anyone, and the written test and selection process are stated to be strictly on merit and transparent. For any grievance or assistance, candidates may email [email protected].

What Are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions. These commissions recruit candidates for various posts and services under state government departments according to the rules applicable to each recruitment.

State PSC recruitment is not limited to State Civil Services examinations. Public Service Commissions may also recruit candidates for engineering, medical, teaching, agriculture, legal, scientific, technical, administrative and other departmental posts.

The posts available depend on vacancies reported by the respective state government departments and the recruitment notifications issued by the commission.

Popular Posts Recruited Through State PSCs

State Public Service Commissions recruit candidates for a wide range of government posts. Common recruitment categories may include:

  • State Civil Services
  • Administrative Services
  • Assistant Commissioner
  • Assistant Director
  • Assistant Professor
  • Lecturer
  • Medical Officer
  • Veterinary Officer
  • Assistant Engineer
  • Assistant Executive Engineer
  • Agriculture Officer
  • Food Safety Officer
  • Drug Inspector
  • Scientific Officer
  • Law Officer
  • Labour Officer
  • Revenue-related Posts
  • Technical Officers
  • Departmental Officers

The actual posts available vary by commission and recruitment notification.

PSC Jobs by Group (Group 1, 2, 2A, 4 & Others)

Several State Public Service Commissions including TNPSC, APPSC, and TSPSC classify recruitment into numbered "Groups" based on post seniority, pay scale, and administrative responsibility. Understanding these groups helps candidates identify which exam to prepare for based on their qualification and career goals.

Group Typical Posts Minimum Qualification Selection Stages
Group 1 Deputy Collector, DSP, Assistant Commissioner, District Registrar Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains + Interview
Group 2 Assistant Section Officer, Tehsildar, Municipal Commissioner (Grade), Block Development Officer Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains (some states include Interview)
Group 2A Junior Assistant, Bill Collector, Field Surveyor Bachelor's degree Written Exam (Certificate Verification)
Group 3 Various department Grade II/Non-Gazetted posts Varies by post Written Exam
Group 4 Junior Assistant, Typist, Steno-Typist, Bill Collector, Record Clerk, Village Administrative Officer (VAO) SSLC / 10th or 12th pass (varies by post) Single Written Exam (Certificate Verification)

Group numbering, post names, and minimum qualifications vary by state the table above reflects the common pattern used by TNPSC-style classification. Some states use different group labels or don't use numbered groups at all. Always confirm the exact group structure and eligibility on your state PSC's official notification.

Who Should Apply for Group 4?

Group 4 posts are typically entry-level government jobs open to candidates who have completed SSLC (10th) or Higher Secondary (12th), making them one of the most accessible and high-demand categories of PSC recruitment. These posts don't usually require a specific degree, have a single-stage written exam, and see some of the highest applicant volumes of any PSC exam due to the lower qualification bar and large number of annual vacancies.

State PSC Eligibility Criteria

There is no single eligibility rule for all State PSC jobs. Qualification, age limit, experience and other conditions differ depending on the commission and post.

Eligibility Criteria General Guidance
Educational Qualification Depends on the post and may include Diploma, Graduation, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Post Graduation or another prescribed qualification.
Age Limit Minimum and maximum age limits vary by commission and recruitment.
Age Relaxation Relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the recruitment.
State / Domicile Conditions State-specific eligibility, reservation, language or residency conditions may apply to certain recruitments.
Experience Some technical, teaching, specialist or senior posts require relevant professional experience.
Number of Attempts Attempt restrictions apply only where specifically prescribed for an examination or recruitment.

Important: Candidates should check the detailed recruitment notification before applying because eligibility conditions differ for every State PSC recruitment.

State PSC Selection Process

The State PSC selection process depends on the commission and the type of post. There is no single selection procedure followed for every PSC recruitment.

Depending on the recruitment, the selection process may include one or more of the following stages:

  • Preliminary Examination
  • Main Examination
  • Written Examination
  • Screening Test
  • Subject-specific Examination
  • Skill Test
  • Physical Test
  • Interview / Personality Test
  • Document Verification
  • Medical Examination

State Civil Services examinations may have Preliminary, Main and Interview stages, while technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitment may follow a different selection process.

Always check the individual recruitment notification for the exact examination and selection procedure.

How to Apply for State PSC Jobs 2026

The application process differs slightly between commissions, but candidates can generally follow these steps:

  1. Find the required State PSC recruitment from the latest jobs table above.
  2. Open the detailed recruitment page.
  3. Check the post name, vacancies, qualification, age limit, application fee and important dates.
  4. Read the official recruitment notification carefully.
  5. Open the official application website or application link.
  6. Complete registration or One-Time Registration if required by the commission.
  7. Enter the required personal, educational and category details.
  8. Upload the prescribed photograph, signature and supporting documents.
  9. Pay the application fee if applicable.
  10. Review the application before final submission.
  11. Submit the application before the specified last date.
  12. Save or print the submitted application for future reference.

Candidates should submit applications only through the application method specified in the official notification.

State PSC Exam Pattern and Syllabus

There is no common exam pattern or syllabus for all State PSC recruitments.

State Civil Services examinations generally cover broader subjects such as General Studies and state-specific topics, while technical, medical, engineering, teaching and departmental recruitment may focus more heavily on subjects related to the post.

The following can differ between recruitments:

  • Number of papers
  • Objective or descriptive examination
  • Total marks
  • Exam duration
  • Negative marking
  • Minimum qualifying marks
  • Language requirements
  • Subject-specific syllabus
  • Interview or skill test requirements

Candidates should refer to the syllabus and exam pattern issued for the specific State PSC recruitment they are applying for.

State PSC Jobs vs UPSC Jobs

State Public Service Commissions and the Union Public Service Commission conduct different recruitment processes.

State PSC UPSC
Conducts recruitment for posts and services connected with the respective state. Conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.
Recruitment rules differ from one State PSC to another. Recruitment is conducted under the rules applicable to UPSC examinations and vacancies.
May recruit for State Civil Services, engineering, medical, teaching, technical and departmental posts. Conducts Civil Services Examination and various other recruitment examinations for Union Government posts.

Candidates looking for Union Government recruitment through UPSC can visit the UPSC Jobs page.

PSC vs PCS - What Is the Difference?

PSC stands for Public Service Commission. It refers to the constitutional commission responsible for conducting recruitment for various government posts and services within its jurisdiction.

PCS commonly refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services posts and examinations.

A State Public Service Commission may conduct a State Civil Services or PCS examination, but it can also conduct recruitment for many other positions such as Medical Officer, Assistant Engineer, Lecturer, Agriculture Officer and departmental posts.

Therefore, State PSC Jobs covers a broader range of recruitment than only PCS or State Civil Services examinations.

How to Choose the Right State PSC Recruitment

Before applying for a State PSC vacancy, candidates should compare the recruitment requirements with their qualification and preferences.

Check the following details:

  • Required educational qualification
  • Age limit
  • Category and reservation conditions
  • State or language requirements, if any
  • Number of vacancies
  • Pay scale or salary
  • Job location
  • Application fee
  • Selection process
  • Examination pattern
  • Application deadline

Apply only after confirming that you meet the eligibility conditions mentioned in the official recruitment notification.

State PSC Recruitment Updates You Should Check

A recruitment notification can sometimes be followed by additional notices from the commission. Candidates should continue checking recruitment updates even after submitting their application.

Important updates may include:

  • Application date extension
  • Correction window
  • Vacancy revision
  • Exam date
  • Exam city information
  • Admit card
  • Answer key
  • Result
  • Interview schedule
  • Document verification schedule
  • Final selection result

Relevant updates should be linked from the individual recruitment page whenever they are released.

Why Check State PSC Jobs on OnlyJobs?

OnlyJobs brings State Public Service Commission recruitment information together in one place so candidates can quickly find current opportunities without checking multiple commission websites individually.

For each recruitment, candidates can find important details such as:

  • Recruiting commission
  • Post name
  • Total vacancies
  • Educational qualification
  • Age limit
  • Salary or pay scale
  • Application fee
  • Selection process
  • Application dates
  • Official notification
  • Official application link

Recruitment information should be checked against the official State Public Service Commission notification before publication. Important corrections, vacancy revisions and date extensions should also be updated whenever they are released.

Latest State PSC Notifications - Frequently Asked Questions

What are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC Jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions for various posts and services under state government departments.

Which State PSC jobs are currently open?

Currently open recruitments are listed in the Latest State PSC Jobs 2026 table at the top of this page. The list is updated when new recruitment notifications and application updates are released.

Where can I find the latest State PSC recruitment notifications?

You can check the latest State PSC recruitment notifications on this page or select your commission from the State-wise PSC Jobs section to find recruitment specific to your state.

What qualification is required for State PSC jobs?

There is no single qualification required for all State PSC jobs. Depending on the post, candidates may need a Diploma, Graduation, Engineering degree, Medical qualification, Law degree, Post Graduation or another specified qualification.

Are all State PSC jobs for graduates?

No. Eligibility depends on the individual recruitment. Many administrative posts require a degree, while technical, professional and departmental posts may have different qualification requirements.

What is the age limit for State PSC jobs?

The minimum and maximum age limits vary according to the commission and post. Candidates should check the age criteria given in the individual recruitment notification.

Is age relaxation available for State PSC recruitment?

Age relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the respective recruitment. The exact relaxation should be checked in the official notification.

Is domicile compulsory for State PSC jobs?

Not for every State PSC recruitment. Some vacancies may have state-specific residency, reservation, language or other eligibility requirements. Candidates should check the relevant recruitment rules before applying.

What is the selection process for State PSC jobs?

The selection process varies by post. It may include a Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, written test, screening test, skill test, interview, physical test, document verification or medical examination.

Do all State PSC recruitments have Prelims and Mains?

No. Prelims and Mains are common in some State Civil Services examinations, but many technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitments follow a different examination or selection process.

How can I apply for State PSC recruitment?

Open the required recruitment from the latest jobs table, read the eligibility and application details, check the official notification and use the official application link provided on the recruitment page.

What is the difference between State PSC and UPSC?

State PSCs conduct recruitment mainly for posts and services connected with their respective states, while UPSC conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.

Is PSC the same as PCS?

No. PSC means Public Service Commission, while PCS generally refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services. A State PSC can recruit for PCS as well as many other administrative, technical, medical and departmental posts.

Where can I check State PSC admit cards?

When an admit card is released, the related recruitment page should be updated with the admit card information and official download link. Candidates can also check the OnlyJobs Admit Card section.

Where can I check State PSC results?

State PSC result updates can be checked through the individual recruitment page or the OnlyJobs Results section.

How often is this State PSC Jobs page updated?

The page is updated when new State PSC recruitment notifications, application extensions and other important recruitment updates become available.

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Most current openings on this page are for Group C posts - Forest Guard, Forester, Beat Guard, and Field Guard - making this a common landing point for anyone searching forest department group c recruitment 2026.

  • Forest Guard - entry-level field post responsible for forest protection and anti-poaching patrols
  • Forester - supervises Forest Guards and manages a forest beat or range sub-unit
  • Forest Beat Officer - field-level post combining patrol, record-keeping, and community liaison duties; commonly searched as forest beat officer notification 2026
  • Range Forest Officer (RFO) - manages an entire forest range, includes administrative and enforcement responsibilities
  • Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) - gazetted officer post, typically recruited through state forest service exams
  • Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer - recruited through UPSC, the highest field-level forestry cadre in India

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs
  • General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics)
  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability
  • Reasoning & Mental Ability
  • State-specific General Knowledge (local geography, forests, wildlife sanctuaries)
  • For Ranger/RFO level: Forestry science, environmental laws, and wildlife protection acts

Note: Apprenticeship posts (under the Apprentices Act) are not regular government jobs but are a popular no-exam entry route into PSUs and railways for ITI/diploma/graduate candidates, offering valuable hands-on experience.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) has announced that the online examination for Generalist and Specialist Officers is tentatively scheduled for Saturday, 31 October 2026. The notice (Ref. No. HRDD/RECT/04B/2026-27) is dated 9 October 2026 and relates to Advertisement No. HRDD/RECT/04/2026-27 for 291 vacancies. 

Direct Link to Check IOB Specialist Officer Exam date 2026

Quick Overview - IOB SO Exam Date 2026

Particulars Details
Conducting body Indian Overseas Bank
Recruitment Generalist / Specialist Officers in various scales, 2026-27
Advertisement number HRDD/RECT/04/2026-27 (dated 28.08.2026)
Exam date notice HRDD/RECT/04B/2026-27 (dated 09.10.2026)
Exam date 31 October 2026 (Saturday), tentatively scheduled
Exam mode Online examination
Total vacancies 291
Grades JMGS I, MMGS II and MMGS III
Official website www.iob.bank.in

IOB SO Exam Date 2026: Official Announcement

The official notice is short. It states that the online examination is tentatively scheduled for 31.10.2026 (Saturday), that admit cards will be made available for download shortly, and that candidates should visit the bank's website regularly for updates.Because the bank uses the word "tentatively", the date can still change. Treat 31 October 2026 as the planned date and re-check iob.bank.in before you travel.

Important Dates

Event Date
Notification released 28 August 2026
Online registration and fee payment start 29 August 2026
Last date to apply and pay fee 15 September 2026
Exam date notice released 9 October 2026
Online exam 31 October 2026 (Saturday)

IOB SO Exam Schedule and Shift Timing

The official notice gives only the date and day. Shift timing, reporting time and gate closing time have not been announced and will be printed on the admit card or call letter.

Detail Information
Exam name IOB Generalist / Specialist Officers online examination
Date and day 31 October 2026, Saturday (tentative)
Total duration 2 hours, with separate timing for each section (per the notification)
Exam centres Allotted through the call letter; see the list below

IOB SO Exam Centres

The notification lists six examination centre cities. The bank may add or remove centres, may allot a centre different from the one you chose, and does not accept requests for change of centre.

  1. Delhi / New Delhi / NCR
  2. Mumbai / Navi Mumbai / MMR / Thane
  3. Chennai
  4. Kolkata
  5. Hyderabad
  6. Bengaluru

IOB SO Vacancy Details 2026

IOB has advertised 291 vacancies. Post Code 01 is the Generalist Officer post and all other posts are Specialist Officer posts. The bank says vacancy numbers are provisional and may be increased or decreased.

IOB SO Eligibility Criteria

Age, qualification and experience are calculated as on 1 August 2026. The table below is a summary. Certification requirements and detailed experience conditions differ by post, so check the full notification for the post you applied for.

IOB SO Exam Pattern 2026

The online exam has 100 objective questions carrying 100 marks, with a total duration of 2 hours and separate timing for each section.

Manager (Branch Management), Scale II

Section Questions Marks Medium Duration
English Language 25 25 English 30 minutes
Professional Knowledge (Banking Law and Practice, Indian Economy and Indian Financial System, Principles and Practices of Banking, Accounting and Financial Management for Bankers) 75 75 English and Hindi 90 minutes
Total 100 100   2 hours

All Other Posts (Scale I, II and III)

Section Questions Marks Medium Duration
English Language 25 25 English 30 minutes
General Awareness with special reference to the Banking Industry 25 25 English 30 minutes
Professional Knowledge (varies post-wise) 50 50 English 60 minutes
Total 100 100   2 hours

Negative Marking and Qualifying Marks

  • One-fourth of the marks for a question are deducted for each wrong answer. There is no penalty for an unattempted question.
  • Overall minimum qualifying marks in the online exam: 35% for unreserved candidates and 30% for reserved candidates.
  • No minimum qualifying marks are prescribed for English Language or General Awareness. Candidates must secure the minimum qualifying marks in Professional Knowledge.

IOB SO Application Fee

Category Fee (inclusive of GST)

All others, including OBC and EWS Rs. 1,000

Required Documents

For the Online Exam

  • Printed call letter / admit card.
  • One original photo identity proof from this list: Passport, Aadhaar / e-Aadhaar, PAN Card, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, Bank Passbook with attested photograph, ID card issued by a school or college, or a Gazetted Officer certificate on official letterhead.
  • A self-attested photocopy of the same ID, to be submitted with the call letter to the invigilator.

A Ration Card is not accepted as ID. If your identity is in doubt or the photocopy is missing, you may not be allowed to appear.

For the Interview Stage (as applicable)

Originals plus self-attested photocopies of the following are required, and candidates may be refused the interview without them:

  • Interview call letter and system-generated printout of the online application.
  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or SSLC / Std. X certificate with date of birth).
  • Photo ID proof.
  • Mark sheets and certificates for educational qualifications, and proof of any preferred certifications.
  • Work experience proof: experience certificates, appointment and relieving letters, pay slips.
  • Category certificates: caste certificate (OBC certificate with non-creamy layer clause, valid on the interview date), EWS income and asset certificate, or PwBD disability certificate, as applicable.
  • No Objection Certificate from the employer, for candidates serving in government, quasi-government or public sector organisations, including nationalised banks and financial institutions.
  • Any other relevant documents supporting eligibility.

How to Apply for IOB SO Recruitment 2026

The application window closed on 15 September 2026. The sources reviewed do not mention any reopening or extension. The steps below are from the official notification, for reference.

  1. Visit www.iob.bank.in and open the Careers page.
  2. Open "Recruitment of Generalist / Specialist Officers in Various Scales - 2026 - 27" and select the post.
  3. Click "Click here to Register Online" and complete registration. A registration number and password are sent by email and SMS.
  4. Upload the photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration as per the specifications.
  5. Fill in the application form and click "Complete Registration".
  6. Pay the application fee online (debit card, credit card, internet banking, BHIM or UPI).
  7. Take a printout of the application form and e-receipt.

How to Check RBI Assistant Mains Result 2026

  1. Visit the official RBI website, rbi.org.in, or the Opportunities Portal at opportunities.rbi.org.in.
  2. Go to the "Opportunities @ RBI" section and open "Current Vacancies" → "Results".
  3. Click on the link for the RBI Assistant Mains Result 2026 (Panel Year 2025).
  4. Download the result PDF to your device.
  5. Open the PDF and press Ctrl+F to search for your roll number.
  6. If your roll number appears in the list, you have qualified for the Language Proficiency Test.

What After RBI Assistant Mains Result 2026?

Candidates shortlisted in the Mains Result must now appear for the Language Proficiency Test (LPT), the final stage of the RBI Assistant selection process. The LPT tests a candidate's ability to read, write, speak, and understand the official/local language of the RBI office for which they applied. Candidates who studied the relevant local language up to the 10th or 12th standard are generally exempted; others must appear for and clear the LPT to remain in contention for final selection. The LPT is qualifying in nature no marks from it are added to the final merit list, but clearing it is mandatory. RBI is yet to announce the exact LPT schedule, venue, and reporting-time details for this cycle; candidates should watch the official portal for this notification.

RBI Assistant Selection Process 2026

  • Preliminary Examination: Qualifying stage only. Prelims marks are not counted towards the final merit list.
  • Main Examination: The Mains score is what decides a candidate's final rank and selection.
  • Language Proficiency Test (LPT): Qualifying stage. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the local/regional language of the RBI office applied for. There is no interview stage in this recruitment.

The Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank), an all-India premier financial institution engaged in financing, facilitating and promoting India's international trade, has invited applications for its Special Recruitment Drive (SRD) for Backlog Vacancies, vide Advertisement No. HRM/DM & M/SRD/2026-27/04.

This Exim Bank Recruitment 2026 covers a total of 8 posts across Deputy Manager (Grade/Scale JM I – Banking Operations) and Manager (Grade/Scale MM II – Internal Audit), against SC, ST, and OBC backlog vacancies. Only Indian citizens are eligible to apply. The online application link will be live from 15 September 2026 to 10 October 2026, and no other mode of application will be accepted. The written examination is tentatively scheduled for November 2026, to be held at Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi, and Guwahati, with personal interviews conducted in Mumbai and New Delhi.

Download Official Notification | Apply Online

Posts Deputy Manager (JM I), Manager (MM II)
Total Vacancies 8

Job Location Anywhere in India (transferable abroad with consent)
Official Website www.eximbankindia.in

Event Date
Website Link Opens 15-09-2026
Last Day for Applying and Payment of Examination Fee 10-10-2026
Tentative Month of Written Examination November 2026*

Note: The exact examination date will be advised through the call letter and updated on the Bank's website. No request for change of centre, venue, date, or session will be entertained.

Exim Bank Deputy Manager & Manager Vacancy 2026

A total of 8 vacancies have been notified under this Special Recruitment Drive for backlog posts, as shown below. Reservations are applicable as per prevailing Government of India guidelines, and the reservation for PwBD candidates is on a horizontal basis for Hearing Impairment (HI) disability.

Position (Grade/Scale) SC ST OBC Total
Deputy Manager (Grade/Scale JM I) 2 1 3 6*
Manager (Grade/Scale MM II) - 2 - 2*

Note: The reservation for PwBD candidates is on a horizontal basis for Hearing Impairment (HI) disability.

Exim Bank Deputy Manager & Manager Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility (age, educational qualification, etc.) is computed as on 31-08-2026, as detailed below for each post.

Manager (Grade/Scale MM II) – Internal Audit (2 Posts)

Qualification: Minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA in Graduation (minimum 3-year full-time course), AND Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) with specialization in Finance / International Business / Foreign Trade, or Chartered Accountant (CA). The Post Graduation course should be a minimum 2-year full-time duration with a specialization in Finance and minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA. For CA, passing the professional examination is sufficient, and membership of ICAI is mandatory.

Experience: Minimum 3 years of experience in a scheduled commercial bank, an all-India financial institution, or another organization of repute, in internal audit / credit audit, including handling preparation and submission of reports by internal/concurrent auditors, audit compliance, analysis and timely submission of audit observations to the audit committee, review of internal/concurrent audit scope and systems/procedures/controls, and experience dealing with RBI on audit/inspection matters (in Scale I or equivalent).

Deputy Manager (Grade/Scale JM I) – Banking Operations (6 Posts)

Qualification: Minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA in Graduation (minimum 3-year full-time course), AND Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) with specialization in Finance / International Business / Foreign Trade, or Chartered Accountant (CA), on the same terms as above.

Experience (as on 31-08-2026): Minimum 1 year of post-qualification (Post Graduation or CA) work experience in a reputed commercial bank / financial institution / state level term lending institution, with skills in project finance, credit appraisal, term lending, analysis of cross-border risks, and financing of overseas joint ventures.

Other Eligibility Notes

  • Candidates should possess excellent communication skills and be proficient in computers and information technology.
  • Candidates from universities awarding CGPA/GPA instead of numerical marks must furnish a conversion letter from the head of the institute / controller of examination if the equivalent percentage is not mentioned on the marksheet.
  • The university/institute must be recognised/approved by the Government / AICTE / UGC.
  • Candidates who completed graduation or post-graduation through correspondence / part-time / open university / open learning / external / distance / e-learning are not eligible.

Exim Bank Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

Age is computed as on 31-08-2026. The maximum age below already includes applicable age relaxation.

Position (Grade/Scale) SC ST OBC (NCL)

Manager (Grade/Scale MM II) 35 35 33

As per Government of India guidelines, the upper age limit for Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) is relaxed by an additional 10 years, and for Ex-servicemen by an additional 5 years.

Exim Bank Deputy Manager & Manager Salary

Position Pay Band (IBA 12th Bipartite Settlement) Approximate Starting Annual CTC
Deputy Manager (Scale JM-I) ₹48480 – 2000 – 62480 – 2340 – 67160 – 2680 – 85920 ₹18 lakh (approximately)
Manager (Scale MM-II) ₹64820 – 2340 – 67160 – 2680 – 93960 ₹20 lakh (approximately)

In addition to pay, selected candidates are eligible for allowances, perquisites, and benefits applicable to the grade as per the Bank's rules prevailing at the time of joining, including residential/leased accommodation (subject to availability) and loan schemes for housing, vehicle, and children's education.

Exim Bank Recruitment 2026 Application Fee

Category Application Fee / Intimation Charges (Non-refundable)
OBC ₹600/-
SC / ST / PwBD / Female candidates ₹100/- (Intimation charges)

Fees are non-refundable, including in cases where the applicant is later found ineligible for the post. Bank transaction charges for online payment must be borne by the candidate. The notification does not separately specify a fee amount for General/Unreserved male candidates.

Exim Bank Deputy Manager & Manager Selection Process

Selection comprises a Written Test followed by a Personal Interview.

Structure of Written Test

Name of Test Section No. of Questions Max. Marks Time
Professional Knowledge – Subjective Part I – Question 1 (Compulsory) 1 40 2 hours 30 minutes
Part II – Attempt any 6 out of 8 Questions 6 (of 8) 60
Total 100 2 hours 30 minutes

There is no sectional cut-off; the final list for interviews is drawn based on the candidate's overall performance in the written test. Final selection is based on combined performance in the Written Examination (out of 100, with 70% weightage) and the Interview (out of 100, with 30% weightage). A pre-recruitment training will be organised for candidates from reserved categories who opt for it through the online application form.

How to Apply for Exim Bank Recruitment 2026

Candidates can apply online only, from 15 September 2026 to 10 October 2026. No other mode of application will be accepted.

  1. Visit the Bank's Online Application page and click "APPLY ONLINE."
  2. Choose "Click here for New Registration" and enter Name, Contact details, and Email ID. A Provisional Registration Number and Password will be generated and also sent via email/SMS.
  3. Fill in the application form; use "SAVE AND NEXT" to save progress before final submission, since no changes are possible after clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION."
  4. Upload your Photograph, Signature, Left Thumb Impression, and Handwritten Declaration as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Fill in remaining details, preview the application, and click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION" only after verifying all details.
  6. Proceed to the "Payment" tab and complete the online fee payment, then click "Submit."
  7. Take a printout of the e-Receipt and the completed online application form for future reference.

Note: Candidates can apply for only one post. If a candidate applies for more than one post, only the latest valid (completed) application/registration will be retained, and fees paid for other registrations will stand forfeited.

Documents and Scanned Images Required

Document Specification
Photograph 4.5cm × 3.5cm, colour, white/light background, 200×230 pixels, 20–50 KB, JPG/JPEG
Signature Black ink on white paper, not in capital letters, 140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB, JPG/JPEG
Left Thumb Impression Black or blue ink on white paper, 240×240 pixels at 200 DPI (3cm × 3cm), 20–50 KB, JPG/JPEG
Handwritten Declaration In English, black ink on white paper, 800×400 pixels at 200 DPI (10cm × 5cm), 50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG
Mark Sheets, Degree Certificates, Experience/Relieving Letter, Caste Certificate (if applicable) PDF format, 20–500 KB

Important Instructions

  • Candidates should be willing to serve anywhere in India; selected candidates may also be transferred to offices outside India with their consent.
  • OBC caste certificates must specifically contain the non-creamy layer clause and must be valid (issued within one year prior to) the last date of applying.
  • Deputy Managers must execute a personal bond of ₹3 lakhs to serve the Bank for a minimum of 5 years from the date of joining.
  • Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or appear in the CIBIL defaulter database are not eligible to join the Bank.
  • Selected candidates already in service must produce a proper relieving letter/discharge certificate in original at the time of joining.
  • Any legal proceedings related to this advertisement can be instituted only in Mumbai, with courts/tribunals in Mumbai having sole and exclusive jurisdiction.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel, restrict, curtail, or enlarge the recruitment process, including the number of vacancies, at any stage without notice.
  • Candidates whose writing speed is permanently affected may use a scribe at their own cost and arrangement, subject to the Bank's stipulated scribe guidelines, and will be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination if registered for it in advance.

Action against misconduct: Candidates found using unfair means, impersonation, misbehaviour in the examination/interview hall, disclosing or transmitting exam content, carrying mobile phones/electronic devices into the hall, or providing false information may be disqualified from the examination, debarred from future Bank examinations, or, if already employed, have their service terminated - in addition to being liable for criminal prosecution.

How to Download SBI PO Mains Admit Card 2026

Credit Auditor Having retired honourably, either superannuated or through VRS (not having been awarded any punishment (major or minor), not charge sheeted & punished for serious lapses/offences in active service). Officers retired as Scale III or above and having minimum experience of 15 years as an Officer in the bank with satisfactory track record including 3 years of experience in dealing with high value credit, project finance, consortium lending, foreign exchange portfolio at Branches or at controlling office/s or as Credit Auditor. When Will the RRB JE City Intimation Slip 2026 Be Released?

The slip is scheduled for release on 17 October 2026. RRBs usually make the city slip available about 10 days before the exam, and the same pattern applies here, since the exam begins on 27 October 2026.

The slip will be available online on the official Railway Recruitment Board portals. A direct download link will be activated only after the release.

How to Download the RRB JE Exam City Intimation Slip 2026

Follow these steps once the link is active:

  1. Visit the official RRB website, www.rrbcdg.gov.in, or the candidate login portal.
  2. Look for the link titled CEN 04/2026 RRB JE CBT 1 City Intimation Slip 2026 in the notice board section.
  3. Enter the login details generated at the time of registration.
  4. Enter the CAPTCHA code and click Submit.
  5. Check your exam city, date and shift on the screen.

Each regional RRB provides its own login link on its official website, so use the website of the RRB to which you applied.

Login Details Required

How to Check RRB JE Application Status 2026

  1. Go to the official application portal, www.rrbapply.gov.in.
  2. Log in with the user credentials you created while applying.
  3. Open your CEN No. 04/2026 application from the dashboard.
  4. View your status: Provisionally Accepted, Conditionally Accepted or Rejected.
  5. If your form is rejected, read the reason shown against your application.
  6. Take a screenshot or printout for your records.

Also Read: SSC MTS and Havaldar Result 2026

Details Needed to Check Your Status

  • The user credentials (login details) created during registration on the RRB application portal
  • Access to the mobile number and email ID you used in the application, to receive status alerts

The official notice does not explain what to do if you have forgotten your login details. If you face this problem, contact the RRB helpdesk listed below.

RRB JE Application Status Meaning: Accepted, Conditionally Accepted and Rejected

Status What it means
Provisionally Accepted Your application met the requirements. You move to the next stage, subject to later verification.
Conditionally Accepted Your application is accepted with conditions. Check the remark in your login and keep the related documents ready.
Rejected Your application was not accepted. The reason is shown in your login.

Important Instructions from the Official RRB Notice

  • Acceptance is not selection. Candidature is provisional and can be cancelled at any stage, even after recruitment, if the data is inconsistent, deficient or false, or in case of any malpractice.
  • No correspondence from rejected candidates. RRB has stated it cannot entertain correspondence from ineligible or rejected candidates.
  • Errors may be corrected. RRB reserves the right to fix any inadvertent, typographical or printing error in the list.
  • Use official sources only. Rely on rrb.indianrailways.gov.in for updates on the recruitment process.
  • Beware of touts. RRB warns against anyone promising selection for money. The process is computerised and selection is based on merit.

What to Do After Checking Your RRB JE Application Status

If your application is accepted

  • Prepare for the Computer Based Test (CBT).
  • Keep checking the official RRB website for the exam city slip and admit card.
  • Keep your certificates ready. Any mismatch with your application can lead to cancellation of candidature later.

If your application is conditionally accepted

  • Read the remark in your login carefully.
  • Keep the documents related to that remark ready.

If your application is rejected

  • Read the rejection reason shown in your login.
  • Note that RRB has said it does not entertain correspondence from rejected candidates.
  • For a technical issue with the status display, you can contact the helpdesk above.
