Things to Know About the Response Sheet

  • Question order may look different. The challenge module shows one fixed sequence of questions and options for all candidates of a shift, while the actual exam showed shuffled sequences.
  • Your answers are still accurate. The options you selected during the exam are shown correctly in the challenge module.
  • Personal use only. The saved question paper is meant for self-analysis, not for sharing.

How to Raise an Objection Against the SSC Selection Post Answer Key

If you believe an answer in the tentative key is wrong, you can challenge it online before 12 October 2026, 4:00 PM. Each challenged question costs ₹50.

  1. Log in to the SSC portal.
  2. Open the Challenge/Objection Management link for Phase-XIV/2026.
  3. Select the question or questions you want to challenge.
  4. Enter your suggested answer and upload supporting documents or a justification.
  5. Pay the ₹50 fee for each question challenged.
  6. Submit the objection before the deadline.

Rules to remember

  • Objections are accepted online only.
  • Objections received after 12 October 2026, 4:00 PM will not be entertained.
  • The final answer key is prepared after reviewing valid objections.
  • Candidates cannot challenge the final answer key.

How to Calculate Your Marks Using the Answer Key

Particulars Marks
Total questions 100
Total marks 200
Correct answer +2
Wrong answer −0.50
Unattempted 0

Formula: Total marks = (Correct answers × 2) − (Wrong answers × 0.50)

Example: A candidate attempts 85 questions, with 70 correct and 15 wrong. Marks = (70 × 2) − (15 × 0.50) = 140 − 7.5 = 132.5.

This is only an estimate. The answer key is tentative, and your score may change if SSC revises any answer after reviewing objections.

What Happens After the SSC Selection Post Answer Key?

  • The objection window closes on 12 October 2026, 4:00 PM.
  • SSC reviews the valid objections.
  • The final answer key is released.
  • The result and category-wise cut-off marks follow.
  • Shortlisted candidates are called for Document Verification.

Example: if a candidate gets 72 answers right, gets 18 wrong and leaves 10 blank, the estimated score is 72 × 2 = 144 out of 200.

  7. Submit the objection and save the acknowledgement, if one is shown.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  1. Objection review: WBPSC examines the objections received during the window.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

The ISS Examination 2026 Statistics papers for which the provisional answer key has been released are:

  • Statistics Paper II - Covers topics including Linear Models, Statistical Inference, Sampling Theory, and Econometrics.

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

UPSC allows candidates to challenge answers in the provisional answer key by submitting a formal representation. The process for raising objections is as follows:

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.
